card.title: 28th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card.flavorText: The 28th Infantry Regiment “Kaniów Riflemen” was based in Łódź and formed part of the Polish Army’s 10th Infantry Division. Together with the 30th and 31st Infantry Regiments and the 10th Light Artillery Regiment, it made up the division’s main combat strength in 1939. The 10th Infantry Division had been created in 1919 from the former Polish 4th Rifle Division and was also headquartered in Łódź. At the outbreak of WWII, it belonged to the Łódź Army under General Franciszek Dindorf-Ankowicz and was tasked with defending the fortified area along the upper Warta River, near the German border. From the morning of 1 September 1939, the division came under heavy attacks by the German Eighth Army, supported by aircraft and artillery. It held its positions until 3 September, when it was ordered to withdraw toward Sieradz. Communication and organizational problems delayed the movement, allowing German troops to cross the Warta. After further fighting against the German 10th and 24th Infantry Divisions, the 10th Division was defeated and scattered by 8 September, although some survivors later crossed the Vistula near Otwock.
